title: The pid-identity tests fail on macOS, where no start time or argv can be read
foundBy: ci run 39376571877, on both macOS legs of build-test

evidence.verified: ci run 39492286708 on 7f5a40a passed, with build-test green on macos-15-intel and on the self-hosted macOS arm64 runner. Both legs had failed these six tests in run 39376571877. On Linux, `go test ./internal/proc ./internal/forward ./internal/engine -count=1` still runs and passes them.

resolution: The six tests skip where /proc is absent. On macOS a record is judged by its pid alone, as R170 allows, so they have nothing to check there. They still run on Linux.
details: Six tests added in f5ada08 expect a recorded process to be told apart by its start time and argv. On macOS `internal/proc` has no `/proc` to read them from, so it judges a record by its pid alone, which R170 allows. The tests fail there: `TestFindTheRecordedProcess`, `TestFindRefusesAnotherProcess` and `TestSignalWithoutAPidfdRechecksTheIdentity` in `internal/proc`, `TestAReusedForwardPidIsDeadAndNeverSignalled` in `internal/forward`, and `TestAReusedVMMPidIsNotTheMicroVM` and `TestAVMMWithAnotherStartTimeIsNotTheRecordedOne` in `internal/engine`. Every push to main fails `ci` until they are fixed.

notes.text: b724833 skips the six tests where /proc is absent. On Linux they still run and pass, and the three packages compile for darwin. The macOS legs of `ci` have not run it yet, so the record stays open until they pass.
